item.title: The Mindgard Philosophy Mindgard’s attacker-aligned, research-driven approach provides security leaders with the insight and operational leverage needed to reduce risk, support compliance, and enable the confident use of AI.
item.description:
Author: Dr. Peter Garraghan
Date: January 12, 2026
Tags: ["AI Security", "Offensive Security", "Cybersecurity Research", "Artificial Intelligence", "Risk Management"]
Summary:
  • Mindgard uses attacker-aligned, research-driven methods to secure AI systems.
  • It originated from research at Lancaster University.
  • The platform emulates attacker behavior to identify AI risks.
  • Mindgard tests entire AI systems, not just models.
  • Continuous research keeps Mindgard ahead of evolving AI threats.
  • It focuses on real security vulnerabilities to reduce risk effectively.

item.title: Evaluatorq: An Open-Source Framework for GenAI Evaluations
item.description:
Author: Ewa Szyszka
Date: January 12, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Software Development", "Machine Learning Evaluation", "Open Source Tools"]
Summary:
  • Evaluatorq is an open-source framework for testing GenAI systems.
  • It supports TypeScript and Python environments.
  • The tool runs evaluations locally or in CI/CD pipelines.
  • It uses jobs, evaluators, and datasets as core components.
  • Users can share data and track model quality via Orq integration.

item.title: Don’t Throw Good Agents After Bad: Smarter Agentic AI Deployment
item.description:
Author: Holistic AI Team
Date: N/A
Tags: ["AI Governance", "AI Risk Management", "Regulatory Compliance", "AI Asset Management", "Enterprise AI Strategy"]
Summary:
  • Organizations face challenges managing AI agents of varying quality.
  • Discarding entire AI systems wastes resources.
  • Effective governance identifies and retains good agents.
  • Tools like Holistic AI help map and audit AI assets.
  • Regulatory frameworks guide ethical AI deployment.
  • Case studies show benefits of holistic AI governance.
